Remember that the scalar triple product $\mathbf{r}\cdot (\mathbf{q}\times \mathbf{p})$ is just the determinant of the matrix whose rows are given by $\mathbf{r},$ $\mathbf{q},$ and $\mathbf{p}.$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf{r}\cdot (\mathbf{q}\times \mathbf{p}) & =\begin{vmatrix}1 & -4 & 1 \\ 3 & -3 & 2 \\ 2 & -1 & 0\end{vmatrix} \\  & =1\cdot \begin{vmatrix}-3 & 2 \\ -1 & 0\end{vmatrix}-(-4)\cdot \begin{vmatrix}3 & 2 \\ 2 & 0\end{vmatrix}+1\cdot \begin{vmatrix}3 & -3 \\ 2 & -1\end{vmatrix} \\  & =((-3)\cdot 0-(-1)\cdot 2)+4(3\cdot 0-2\cdot 2)+(3\cdot (-1)-2\cdot (-3)) \\  & =2-16+3 \\  & =-11.\end{aligned}
$$
